model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: an incumbent in a Democratic-leaning district with a nearly 500-to-1 fundraising advantage, and markets pricing a Democratic win at roughly 96%. With no polls or expert ratings offering any contrary evidence, there is little basis to move off a Safe Democratic rating.
model.watch: A sharply unfavorable national environment or a sudden influx of outside spending for the challenger could narrow what is otherwise a quiet, low-information contest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
Delaware's at-large House seat sits in territory that leans Democratic by about eight points, and first-term incumbent Sarah McBride is running for re-election. No public general-election polls are available and no expert race raters cover the contest, so the picture rests on structural factors. Prediction markets put Democratic chances near 96%.

The money gap is stark: McBride has raised about $5.6 million and holds $2.3 million on hand, while Republican Joseph Arminio has raised roughly $12,000 with under $7,000 available, and outside spending is negligible. With an incumbent seeking a second term, a favorable district lean, and a challenger lacking resources or visible campaign activity, the race rates as Safe Democratic. The main uncertainty is the absence of polling, which leaves some room for surprise in an unusually low-information contest.
